summary: The opening Neow blessing made the first three fights harmless, but the run then lost substantial HP across later combats and reached Gremlin Nob at only 33 HP. The most actionable failure was the Nob fight: several skills were used while Nob was already threatening attacks, leaving insufficient energy for the strongest attacks and ending the run at 19 HP with Nob still at 30 HP. The final deck also leaned heavily toward attacks and setup without adding much defensive capacity.

lessons.title: Treat Gremlin Nob skills as a major cost
lessons.situation: When fighting Gremlin Nob, especially after HP has fallen below half and Nob is attacking, reassess every skill before playing it.
lessons.lesson: Minimize nonessential skills against Nob and prioritize a direct attack or a clearly necessary block. Avoid spending a turn on multiple setup skills that leave the strongest attacks unplayable, since Nob punishes skill-heavy turns.
evidence_points: On turn 4 at 19/80 HP, the agent played Battle Trance, then Thunderclap, then Armaments, and finally used its last energy on Defend while Gremlin Nob remained at 30 HP.
Earlier, on turn 3 at 23/80 HP, the agent played Searing Blow+1 and Strike without gaining block, and Nob continued attacking while only partially damaged.
The fight ended at 19/80 HP with Gremlin Nob still at 30/86 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The logged sequence shows repeated setup and skill use during a lethal-pressure fight, while the resulting energy state prevented the available high-damage cards from being used. Against Nob, this pattern both increases his strength through skills and delays ending the fight.

lessons.title: Do not keep adding damage cards when the deck lacks resilience
lessons.situation: After the early rewards have already supplied several attacks and setup cards, particularly when HP is falling through Act 1.
lessons.lesson: Prefer skipping speculative damage/build-around cards when no clearly efficient defensive option is offered, rather than continuing to add attacks that do not solve incoming damage. Build enough reliable defense or mitigation to preserve HP for elites and the boss.
evidence_points: The final 17-card deck contained five Strikes, four Defends, Searing Blow+1, Perfected Strike, Thunderclap, Clothesline, Headbutt, Armaments, and Battle Trance; the only permanent basic block cards were the four Defends plus Armaments.
The run's HP fell from 71/80 after floor 5 to 32/80 after floor 7, then reached 27/80 after floor 8.
The later reward choices added Perfected Strike and Thunderclap after Searing Blow had already been taken and upgraded.
lessons.reasoning: The final list confirms a damage- and setup-heavy deck without a substantial new defensive package, while the HP trajectory shows that this imbalance mattered before the elite. Since skipping was available at the later rewards, declining marginal attack cards would have been a safer default when they did not address survivability.
